one_liner: Notion has a broad REST API with free self-serve internal tokens, PATs and public OAuth, plus an official hosted MCP server; ready to build.
auth_notes: Public connections use OAuth 2.0 authorization code (token endpoint uses Basic client auth). Internal connection API tokens and personal access tokens are static bearer tokens.
access_notes: Integrations can be created on any plan including Free. Internal connections need workspace owner; PATs can be created by owners on a free workspace.
blocker_notes: No meaningful blocker; internal connections require workspace owner, which a free personal workspace provides.

evidence.quote: personal access tokens use a user-scoped static token, and OAuth integrations and public integrations use the OAuth 2.0 protocol.
There’s no OAuth flow to implement — you get a token immediately when you create the connection, and you use that same token for every API request.
Create a public connection so each user can authorize access with OAuth.
You can create an integration on any of the four plans, so your plan tier doesn't restrict your ability to build integrations
A bearer token is required to interact with the Notion API.
Read, create, update, and search content; read and create comments; and read supported user information through Notion’s REST API.
Notion MCP is a remote MCP server hosted by Notion.
